kf: **Papular urticaria** is a persistent itchy hypersensitivity reaction to insect bites (fleas, bed bugs, mites, mosquitoes).
Grouped or linear ('breakfast, lunch and dinner') papules, sometimes with central punctum or blisters, on exposed skin or ankles.
Commonest in children aged 2–10; other household members may be unaffected.
Eradicate the source (treat **all pets**, professional pest control for bed bugs); antihistamine and mild–moderate topical steroid.
Most bites do not need antibiotics; treat only clear secondary infection.

sub: Children, newcomers to a household, travellers; tolerance develops with ongoing exposure.

aet: Type I and IV hypersensitivity to insect saliva antigens.
myths: **"Only one child is affected, so it can't be bites"**: sensitivity varies between people.
patho_lead: The rash is an **allergic reaction to insect saliva**, not the bite itself.

mech.t: The insect injects saliva containing anticoagulant and enzyme proteins.
IgE on mast cells triggers a wheal within minutes.
T cells respond over 24–48 hours, producing a firm itchy papule that lasts days to weeks.
mech.cap: Clusters of bites on the ankle.

histo: Wedge-shaped perivascular infiltrate with eosinophils; rarely needed.

sub: Linear bites on the face, neck and arms; blood spots on sheets; professional eradication needed.

comp: Impetigo, scarring, post-inflammatory pigmentation, sleep disturbance.
prog: Settles when the source is removed; children grow out of it.
